samples.summary: New view wiring (clear copy buffer only when paste succeeds) has no test in either view
samples.evidence: Both `Worksheet.pasteData` (worksheet.ts:4899) and `Spreadsheet` (spreadsheet.ts:~715) changed from unconditional `clearCopyBuffer()` to `if (await paste(...)) clearCopyBuffer()`. Grepping the whole sheets test tree for `clearCopyBuffer|handlePaste|pasteFromClipboard` finds only packages/sheets/test/sheet/clipboard.test.ts:357 (a model-level test of clearCopyBuffer itself). The only view harness that touches paste, packages/sheets/test/view/worksheet-keymap.test.ts:59, mocks it as `paste: vi.fn()` which resolves to `undefined` — i.e. falsy — so the new branch would be silently exercised in the wrong direction and no assertion would notice if the condition were inverted or dropped. The user-visible behavior claimed in the new comments (marching ants stay up, retry possible) is untested.

samples.summary: No test asserts paste() returns true on a successful paste — only the two refusal paths are asserted
samples.evidence: `paste` newly returns a boolean the views use to decide whether to clear the copy buffer. The only return-value assertions in the suite are `expect(await sheet.paste({ text })).toBe(false)` (merge.test.ts:211) and `.toBe(false)` (merge.test.ts:254). Every other paste call site (clipboard.test.ts:113–673, merge.test.ts:104/125/141/165/187/234/276/301/319/335/351/364) ignores the result. A regression where paste always returned false (or undefined) would keep the whole suite green while breaking cut-paste-once and marching-ants clearing in the views.

samples.summary: Live re-read of source merges is only tested for the unmerge case, not the shiftCells/moveRows/moveColumns cases the comment names, nor the merge-created-after-copy case
samples.evidence: The comment at sheet.ts:2192-2195 justifies reading merges live because 'a snapshot survives `shiftCells`, `moveRows`/`moveColumns` and `unmergeSelection`'. Only the unmerge path is covered (merge.test.ts:217 'should not re-create a merge unmerged after the copy'). No test in packages/sheets/test (merge.test.ts, clipboard.test.ts, shifting.test.ts, moving.test.ts) copies a merged range and then shifts/moves rows or columns before pasting, nor covers the newly-enabled inverse (a block merged after the copy now being reproduced at the destination). Those are the paths where the live read differs most from the old snapshot.
searchedFor: glob packages/sheets/test/**/*.ts (shifting.test.ts, moving.test.ts present but no copy+paste merge cases)

samples.summary: The defensive span clone `{ ...m.span }` is not covered by any test
samples.evidence: paste() now copies the span object (`span: { ...m.span }`) so source and destination blocks are independent. No test in merge.test.ts mutates one block's span (e.g. via a subsequent merge/insertRows on the destination) and asserts the source block is unchanged, so aliasing could be reintroduced without any test failing.
searchedFor: grep rangeOf / span usage in packages/sheets/src

samples.summary: Empty-input paste early returns (no text/html, empty grid) have no test asserting the new false return
samples.evidence: paste() has three false-returning early exits for empty input: the pivot guard (line ~2166), the `else { return false; }` when neither text nor html is present, and `if (!pasteRange && grid.size === 0) return false;` (line 2254, replacing the old gridRange()-undefined check). No test calls `sheet.paste({})` or pastes an empty string/empty HTML table and asserts `false`; pivot-protection.test.ts checks paste is ignored but (per grep) without asserting the return value. The views now key buffer clearing off this return, so the empty-input contract is unverified.
